purpose: Headless whole-file build of the genuine linuxdoom-1.10 input path (event queue, responders, G_BuildTiccmd, the defaults table, G_Ticker with the demo write and re-read, and the X translation of i_video.c against a declared fake Xlib), driven by event scripts. Expected commands come from the genuine code only, never from Rust output. No WAD is read.

M_LoadDefaults stores every default through int*; the string rows (chat macros, mousedev, mousetype, sndserver) need the whole pointer under LP64. Rows are classified as M_SaveDefaults does (m_misc.c:320-321); integer rows are stored exactly as the genuine line stores them. The input path reads none of the string rows.

G_DoLoadLevel clears sizeof(mousebuttons) bytes, the size of the pointer boolean* (g_game.c:187): 4 bytes on the 32-bit original, which clears mousebuttons[0] (fire) only, and 8 under LP64, which also clears mousebuttons[1] (strafe); observed in the Phase 1 prototype (loadlevel_mouse_strafe_x, strict against strict32). sizeof(boolean) is the ILP32 count (an enum of 4 bytes). Owner ruling S11: declared so that the LP64 builds agree with the 32-bit original.
as g_game.c:495 for joybuttons (boolean*, g_game.c:204); no joystick event is ever posted, so it cannot show.

behaviour: Headers: only the declarations the genuine i_video.c uses, with the X11 protocol values of the event types, masks, buttons and keysyms; errnos.h stands for <errnos.h>, named by i_video.c:48 and absent from current systems (it includes <errno.h>; i_video.c uses nothing from it).
Event queue: a FIFO of scripted XEvents drained by XPending and XNextEvent (i_video.c:309-312).
Keys: the fake keycode is the keysym the script named; XKeycodeToKeysym (d, keycode, 0) returns it (i_video.c:102); any other index aborts.

Pointer: the window position and the held-button mask; a ButtonPress or ButtonRelease carries the state before it and a MotionNotify the current state (the X protocol rule i_video.c:214-251 relies on).
XWarpPointer (i_video.c:323-328) is counted; with `config warpmodel 1` a warp that moves the pointer queues a MotionNotify at the destination ahead of the next tic's events.
Every other Xlib entry point is reachable only from I_InitGraphics, I_FinishUpdate and I_ShutdownGraphics, which the driver never calls, and aborts.

driver_behaviour: Start-up (d_main.c:1015, 1092, 1110, 1113, 356-357): myargc 1 (or `-config m5b_input.cfg` when the script has `config set` lines, which the driver writes to that file in the working directory; string values are refused, so the LP64 pointer store of m_misc.c:392-393 is never reached); gamemode registered; language english; M_LoadDefaults; M_Init; HU_Init; ST_Init; single-player globals; X_display = the fake display, X_width 320, X_height 200; with recording (the default) G_RecordDemo ("m5binput"), G_InitNew (sk_medium, 1, 1), G_BeginRecording. basedefault is never filled (IdentifyVersion is not called), so without `config set` no file is read and the defaults are the genuine table (m_misc.c:236-297).

Per tic, the singletics branch of D_DoomLoop (d_main.c:376-386): I_StartTic; D_ProcessEvents; G_BuildTiccmd (&netcmds[consoleplayer][maketic%BACKUPTICS]); if (advancedemo) D_DoAdvanceDemo; M_Ticker; G_Ticker; gametic++; maketic++. Scripted X events are queued in the fake server before the tic; `ev` lines call D_PostEvent when read.
Observers (-Wl,--wrap) of D_PostEvent and the five responders record each delivered event and which responder ate it, then call the genuine function; they never change an event or a verdict.

Golden rows (tests/reference/m5b_input/README.md): h (demo header), s (state vector when it changes), L (loadlevel), e (delivered event and its taker), q (posted and delivered counts when they differ), t (per tic: the built command at full 16-bit angleturn before the demo round trip, the executed command after it, the four demo bytes, turnheld capped at 6, the two double-click state machines with their timers capped at 21, the mouse button array and the held keys), r (run length of identical t rows), c (nonzero consistancy or chatchar), x (I_Error or I_Quit) and z (end).

`loadlevel` calls G_DoLoadLevel between tics (g_game.c:489-496), as G_Ticker does for ga_loadlevel; `enddemo` calls G_CheckDemoStatus (g_game.c:1676-1683), which writes m5binput.lmp in the working directory and ends with I_Error.
Test-only options: --selftest-cmd TIC flips bit 0 of one built forwardmove after G_BuildTiccmd; --selftest-drop-event N does not post the N-th posted event. Neither changes genuine code text.

golden_row_kinds.h: HEX: the 13 demo header bytes after G_BeginRecording (recording only)
golden_row_kinds.s: TIC STATE: the state vector (comma-separated name=value) at start (TIC -1) and whenever it changes
golden_row_kinds.L: TIC: a loadlevel directive ran before tic TIC
golden_row_kinds.e: TIC TYPE DATA1 DATA2 DATA3 WHO: an event delivered by D_ProcessEvents in tic TIC; key events print DATA2 and DATA3 as -; WHO is M (M_Responder ate it), g (G_Responder returned before HU/ST/AM), H, S, A (that responder ate it) or G (it reached G_Responder's switch)
golden_row_kinds.q: TIC POSTED DELIVERED: printed only when they differ (events lost to the MAXEVENTS ring, d_main.c:150-154)
golden_row_kinds.t: TIC F S A B XF XS XA XB DEMO TURNHELD DCT DCS DCL DCT2 DCS2 DCL2 MB KEYS
golden_row_kinds.r: N: the previous t row repeats N more times, its tic advancing by one each time
golden_row_kinds.c: TIC C H XC XH: built and executed consistancy and chatchar, only when one is nonzero
golden_row_kinds.x: TIC KIND MESSAGE: I_Error or I_Quit (the run stops; a q or limit end records no t row for that tic)
golden_row_kinds.z: TIC DEMOLEN: the script ended normally before tic TIC; DEMOLEN is demo_p - demobuffer, or -1 when not recording
